subject: Tier-blend pricing & seat-smoothing proposal — Medisys
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@medisys.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.porter@medisys.com
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry — tier blending / seat smoothing options for upcoming rollout

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We’re trying to lock in the commercial structure for our pilot in Q4 and have two specific asks:

- We need guidance on mixing seats across two tiers (standard + reserved) to hit predictable latency without overcommitting GPU capacity.
- Medisys would like a "seat-smoothing" option so usage spikes don’t result in sudden billing jumps — ideally some buffer credits or averaged billing across the month.

I attached a rough forecast and SOW (MA_Pricing_2027Q3.xlsx, Medisys_SOW_Draft.pdf) — can you share recommended pricing approaches and whether Redwood can support a blended-tier rate plus a short-term smoothing credit?

Also, quick call? Alex and I are free Wed 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Emma Li
VP, Engineering
Medisys Health

Attachment(s): MA_Pricing_2027Q3.xlsx (XLSX), Medisys_SOW_Draft.pdf (PDF)

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma.li@medisys.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@medisys.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — tier blending / seat smoothing options for upcoming rollout

Hi Emma — great to meet earlier. Thanks for the files.

High-level suggestions up front:
1) Tier-blend model: price reserved seats at a discounted commit rate, let standard seats float (pay-as-you-go). We can route latency-critical traffic to reserved GPUs and fallback lower-priority traffic to standard. We’ll provide a single blended per-token price for your monthly invoice so you see one number.

2) Seat-smoothing credit: we can offer a three-part approach — a smoothing credit pool (applies to monthly overages), an averaging window (7-day rolling average), and a small committed burst allowance. That avoids per-spike bill shocks.

3) Transition credit: for customers consolidating tiers mid-quarter we typically provide a one-time transitional credit to limit churn costs.

I put together a proposal matrix and a preliminary pricing sketch in the attached spreadsheet. Can Ben sign off on the discount band? Marcus, are there any guardrails we need to impose on routing or KV cache behavior for mixed-tier requests?

Happy to take Wed 10am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): MA_Pricing_2027Q3.xlsx (updated sheet)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tier-blend pricing & seat-smoothing proposal — Medisys

Priya / Marcus —

Looked through the forecast and the sketch. We can approve a commercial package along these lines, subject to a couple of conditions:

- Max headline discount to Medisys should be 15% off list for blended pricing, plus a one-time migration credit equivalent to 5% of the first invoice (applied as account credit).
- Offer a 60-day smoothing credit window rather than 7 days — that’s more conservative for capacity planning.
- No permanent inclusion of beta features (e.g., experimental quantization paths) in the baseline reserved tier; we can include a limited trial for 90 days as part of the kickoff.

If Priya thinks they need >15% we should ask for an incremental commitment (longer term or higher commit). Marcus: confirm operational impact of a 60-day smoothing window on autoscaler behavior.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Note: this is approval in principle — legal to manage final SLA and contract language.

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, Emma Li <emma.li@medisys.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tier-blend pricing & seat-smoothing proposal — Medisys

On Mon, Aug 16, 2027 at 09:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Emma — great to meet earlier. Thanks for the files.
>
> High-level suggestions up front:
> 1) Tier-blend model: price reserved seats at a discounted commit rate, let standard seats float (pay-as-you-go).

Quick note on implementation: a 60-day smoothing window is feasible but we need to enforce two technical guardrails to avoid unpredictable cold-starts:
- Prefetch policy: reserve a small async pre-warm budget for top-N prefixes to minimize latency when traffic moves from standard->reserved.
- KV cache affinity: pinned keys for QPS-heavy endpoints so cache locality is preserved across blended routing.

Operationally, with the proposed migration credit we can set the autoscaler to treat the smoothing pool as a soft buffer. No code changes required, but size the buffer conservatively for the first month and we'll iterate.

Also: Priya, when you present pricing, include a clear rollback (downgrade) step with proration — customers like a simple seat exchange flow.

Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma.li@medisys.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@medisys.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-17T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal: blended-tier pricing + smoothing credit (action required)

Emma / Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary:
- Headline blended price: list price less 15% (applies to blended invoice across reserved + standard use).
- One-time migration credit: 5% of first invoice applied to account (visible on month+1 invoice).
- Smoothing policy: 60-day rolling average billing with a 10% monthly buffer pool (applies to token overages up to the pool).
- Trial: include access to experimental quantization path for up to 90 days (no SLA change).
- Operational guardrails: prefetch policy + KV cache affinity as discussed.

Action items:
- Emma: confirm acceptance of the headline commercial terms and whether Medisys can commit to a 12-month minimum spend target (we’ll need that for the 15% discount).
- Alex: confirm the SOW attachment and any procurement timing constraints — if you want, I’ll generate a draft term sheet and open the DocuSign envelope.
- Ben & Marcus: pending legal review, this is go-to-contract if Medisys accepts the above.

If you’d like to move forward, I’ll prepare a short term sheet and route to legal + DocuSign (link below will be populated once you confirm).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0119
